problem: The new sort on raw weights returns shares ordered by weight (largest first) instead of in input order, so money goes to the wrong recipients (allocate("10", ["1","3"]) returns [7.50, 2.50] instead of [2.50, 7.50]); the same sort also raises TypeError on mixed int/str/Decimal weights that main accepts, and compares string weights as text ("9" > "10").

The bare `import reference_impl` makes production code depend on a module named as a test reference and resolved through sys.path, so any same-named file earlier on the path (for example in the working directory) silently replaces the allocation logic.

`list(weights)` now runs before amount and places are checked, so invalid input raises a different exception than before (allocate("-1", None) raises TypeError instead of ValueError("amount must not be negative")).
Nothing tests `allocate`: no check of output order against input order, mixed-type weights, ties or generator input, and a single test with distinct weights would have caught F1.
`from fractions import Fraction` is no longer used (ruff F401).
`_to_decimal` is never called and duplicates reference_impl.py:5-12, so the two copies of the validation can drift apart.
`Decimal` is imported only for the dead `_to_decimal` helper.
